title: Signs and Similitudes
notes: This chunk delivers a dense, assertive chain of lived similitudes—Abraham’s offering, Joseph’s life, Rahab’s scarlet line, and Israel’s history fulfilled in the Son—with tight scripture links and no hedging. The Abraham-to-John and Joseph-to-Stephen sequences land with force, and the Clement citation seals the Rahab reading cleanly. House-style sentence-open violations (And, That) and residual presenter staging (scenes, lens) interrupt the prose rhythm. One relative clause lacks its connector and tangles a cross-reference. Surgical fixes restore flow and register without touching doctrine, quotes, or the author’s law-positive density.

proposals.old: And Abraham names the place with a promise in the future tense: __“In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen”__ (Genesis 22:14).
proposals.new: Abraham names the place with a promise in the future tense: __“In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen”__ (Genesis 22:14).
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with And.

proposals.old: That is a similitude: not a story about the truth, but the truth rehearsed.
proposals.new: This is a similitude: not a story about the truth, but the truth rehearsed.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with That; This preserves the tight claim.

proposals.old: And then the line Stephen preached to the Sanhedrin: __“at the *second time* Joseph was made known to his brethren”__ (Acts 7:13).
proposals.new: Then the line Stephen preached to the Sanhedrin: __“at the *second time* Joseph was made known to his brethren”__ (Acts 7:13).
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with And; Then keeps the sequence.

proposals.old: (1 Corinthians 10:2, a crossing the sym:sym-sea[Sea & Waters] chapter will read)
proposals.new: (1 Corinthians 10:2, a crossing that the sym:sym-sea[Sea & Waters] chapter will read)
proposals.rationale: The appositive lacks its connector and reads as a fragment; that restores grammar without altering sense or markup.

proposals.old: Now widen the lens all the way, because the master similitude is Israel herself.
proposals.new: The master similitude is Israel herself.
proposals.rationale: Now widen the lens is presenter staging; the claim stands cleanly on its own.

proposals.summary: Drop leading Now from staging line.
proposals.rationale: Avoids residual presenter register at the open while preserving the author’s scene metaphor.
